5. Aggregate Demand

What survives when individual demands are added up — the properties of aggregate demand and the representative consumer.

  • Aggregating Demand — Add three consumers’ Cobb-Douglas demand curves into one aggregate curve. Walras’ law and homogeneity of degree zero survive — move each demand and check.
  • The Representative Consumer — Shift wealth between two identical-taste consumers however you like — the aggregate demand curve never moves. When demand depends only on total wealth, a representative consumer exists.
